referenceCues.source: locked Project Gorgon review set (local, non-redistributed)

conceptPromptProvenance.exactPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production modeling reference sheet for a real-time game house, to guide Blender authoring; not a final render
Primary request: create one cohesive high-fidelity architectural concept sheet for an asymmetric late-medieval temperate hall-house at the visual quality of a premium handcrafted fantasy RPG environment
Subject: a 9.6 by 7.2 meter one-and-a-half-storey hall-house with an asymmetric cross-gable service bay, offset fieldstone chimney, steep layered slate roof, one dormer, deep eaves, continuous irregular stone foundation, and a small covered timber stoop
Composition/framing: a clean four-panel reference sheet showing (1) exterior three-quarter hero view, (2) straight-on front elevation, (3) close doorway and recessed window construction detail, and (4) furnished main-hall interior looking toward the entrance; consistent architecture and proportions in every panel
Materials/textures: thick aged lime-plaster walls over coherent structural oak framing, genuinely recessed window apertures with deep plaster/stone reveals, beveled timber jambs and mullions, 2x3 leaded glass panes with varied cool reflections, layered overlapping slate courses and ridge caps, irregular mortared fieldstone, modeled joinery and ironwork, construction-aware damp/runoff/soot/wear, substantial tactile surface depth
Functional details: clearly modeled thick oak plank-and-frame front door shown partly open around 70 degrees on visible iron strap hinges and hinge knuckles; clean wall opening with no texture overlap; raised dry stone-and-oak threshold; unobstructed one-meter traversal aisle; visible warm furnished interior with hearth, table, benches, shelves, textiles, tools, floorboards, rafters
Style/medium: polished 3D game-environment concept art with physically plausible construction, cohesive art direction, high geometric detail, readable silhouettes, realistic material response; grounded medieval fantasy, not whimsical
Lighting/mood: neutral overcast daylight for material readability, restrained warm interior bounce, no dramatic darkness
Constraints: all four panels depict exactly the same house; model-sheet clarity; no people; no labels or text; no watermark; no UI; no cutaway that breaks exterior consistency
Avoid: Minecraft or voxel windows, face-mounted glass rectangles, flat roof slabs, uniformly repeated stone blocks, universal procedural noise, low-poly primitives, empty shell interior, exaggerated cartoon proportions, texture seams crossing apertures, photobashing incoherence

avoid: treating concept pixels as texture source

prompt.intent: Generate a production cottage that remains mechanically functional in Limina while meeting the locked built-environment visual floor.
prompt.text: Author a cohesive asymmetric late-medieval hall-house with a cross-gable service bay, offset fieldstone chimney, dormer, covered stoop, thick layered walls, continuous foundation, constructed slate courses, deeply recessed leaded windows, a clean portal with a visibly hinged 95-degree inward oak door, raised dry threshold, and a complete furnished interior; preserve the exact Limina functional-building semantic contract.

targetEngineViews.purpose: primary exterior and unmistakable open leaf
hinge, leaf sweep, raised threshold, and portal clearance detail
firebox depth, fuel stack, flame separation, mantel joinery, and local exposure
25 metre silhouette, material breakup, and LOD stability

constructionResponse.summary: Authored the asymmetric 9.6x7.2m functional hall-house, statically batched three geometric LODs, and produced a KHR_texture_basisu-only production GLB with 30 KTX2 textures.
changes: asymmetric cross-gable massing
visible 70-degree hinged door
furnished traversable interior
LOD0/1/2 static batches
extension-only KTX2 PBR textures

critiqueFindings.finding: Production KTX2 normal maps used toktx --normal_mode, but the standard Three glTF normal shader does not reconstruct Z from that two-channel representation; all surfaces exhibited severe diagonal lighting bands.
The interior camera looked outward and clipped the wall/window instead of proving furnishings and the clear aisle.

decision.reason: The exact engine capture exposed an incompatible normal-map channel encoding and a non-reviewable interior view.

constructionResponse.summary: Preserved conventional RGB tangent-space normals through KTX2 production and corrected the interior review direction while retaining the exact functional v4 geometry and LOD chain.
changes: removed incompatible two-channel normal encoding
added decoded normal-direction regression gate
reframed interior view toward furnishings and traversal aisle
strengthened guarded output provenance

decision.reason: CPU decode proves conventional RGB tangent normals with bounded angular error; visual acceptance still requires a fresh guarded engine capture.

constructionResponse.summary: Rebuilt the focal opening construction from the Blender source so every certified window is physically exposed, deeply recessed, and clear through the complete opaque scene geometry.
changes: moved the dormer assembly from its erroneous ground-floor elevation into the dormer
split the south roof sheathing, slate skin, and courses around a real dormer penetration
added dormer cheek walls and paired roof planes
removed the cross-bay-occluded decorative south-east window and opened the hall-to-service-bay connection
made facade timber framing opening-aware instead of crossing window apertures
aligned the chimney stack with the authored hearth and removed the conflicting north-east window
moved interior shelving clear of the west window reveal
added all-opaque-triangle exterior and inward aperture corridor verification

critiqueFindings.finding: Exterior plaster and timber retain strong repetitive diagonal/banded texture response that reads procedurally tiled rather than weathered construction.
Leaded panes read as coarse opaque blue grids with block-scale cells and insufficient glass/reflection depth.
The open portal reveals terrain vegetation and an exterior-lit opening instead of a sealed, coherent furnished room; production ground cover also intrudes across the interior floor.
Foundation and threshold remain visibly box-assembled with coarse repeated blocks and weak joinery hierarchy at the required detail distance.
LOD1 triangle decimation destroys the roof: large holes, floating slate strips, and broken dormer/slope surfaces are visible at 25 metres.

decision.reason: The exact guarded GB10 engine set fails the locked built-environment floor in material coherence, interior enclosure, threshold craft, window response, and silhouette-preserving LOD integrity.

constructionResponse.summary: Replaced the rejected procedural texture system with six hash-pinned Poly Haven CC0 PBR packs, authored phase-continuous exported UV0, transparent leadlight, site exclusion, topology-safe LODs, and more construction-resolved portal, chimney, door, and window geometry.
changes: removed synthesized sine/checker texture generation from the Blender authoring path
embedded six source-manifest hashes covering plaster, fieldstone, grey roof tile, medieval brick, structural oak, and worn plank PBR packs

replaced opaque textured glazing with restrained standard glTF alpha-blended glass and modeled diamond leadwork
split the foundation around the portal and rebuilt the approach as staggered individual stone steps
added an articulated housed diagonal door brace and staggered chimney face masonry
resolved the complete rotated building footprint against terrain and excluded discrete and continuous vegetation before population mount
replaced triangle deletion with whole-primitive semantic LOD filtering
added adversarial UV-phase and opaque-glass regression failures plus exact KTX source/payload closure

critiqueFindings.finding: The terrain-valid footprint is visibly placed in the river; relief-only placement authority does not prove a dry buildable site.
The selected clay-plaster albedo reads as uniform ochre-brown rather than aged pale lime plaster, collapsing wall/timber separation.
Structural posts, jambs, and rails show strong cross-member zebra bands because the source grain axis is mapped perpendicular to member length.
The door leaf, furniture, and floor repeat coarse striped/checkered plank cells rather than coherent authored boards and joinery.
Diamond leadwork and framing remain too heavy and black at hero distance, obscuring the glazing instead of reading as fine came construction.
The room remains dark, sparse, and box-assembled, without the warm lived-in prop and lighting hierarchy required by the locked concept floor.

decision.reason: The guarded GB10 evidence set proves the new material/LOD pipeline works, but site eligibility, color separation, timber orientation, leadwork scale, and interior authorship still fail the locked built-environment floor.

constructionResponse.summary: Corrected the rejected site, palette, timber orientation, interior illumination, and doorway construction while preserving the Blender-authored functional hierarchy and production engine pipeline.
changes: moved the review placement to the nearest dry footprint-valid site and deepened the continuous foundation plinth for measured terrain relief
replaced ochre clay plaster with hash-pinned Poly Haven white plaster for pale lime wall, mortar, and interior roles
mapped timber grain along each member's longest local axis and introduced a dedicated door-oak material role

reduced lead-came thickness while retaining the contracted diamond-pane construction

corrected the segmented-step endpoint arithmetic that more than doubled and miscentered both threshold courses
increased the inward functional sweep from 70 to 95 degrees so the real rendered leaf parks at the hinge edge

critiqueFindings.finding: Exported practical lights reach roughly 978 to 1902 candela without bounded ranges, clipping 60.3% of threshold pixels and every interior pixel in at least one channel; material and furnishing response is not reviewable.
The projecting cross-gable floor extends beyond the main subfloor and perimeter foundation without its own closed plinth or masonry return, leaving the bump-out corner visibly broken and unsupported.
Modeled slate course lips compete with the base roof texture and begin reading as perpendicular horizontal boards across the lower slope instead of one coherent overlapping shingle system.
The service-bay gable apex rises through the cross-roof skin rather than terminating below the roof underside with a clean rake/verge closure.

decision.reason: The guarded GB10 evidence proves the doorway repair, but unbounded practical-light conversion, an unsupported service-bay base, incoherent roof courses, and a gable-through-roof penetration remain below the locked construction and material floor.

constructionResponse.summary: Closed the rejected service-bay construction, roof junction, roof mapping, and practical-light exposure defects while retaining the proven functional doorway and production-engine review path.
changes: added a continuous deep stone service-bay subfloor core plus exposed masonry front and side returns, with the main foundation segmented around the overlap
lowered and closed the service-bay wall construction against its new support instead of leaving a visible floating corner
removed the duplicate modeled roof-course bars that read as perpendicular boards across the lower slopes

reduced the three Blender practical-light energies to bounded exported candela values and authored finite ranges
added sampled occupied-space illuminance limits and guarded post-capture pixel clipping rejection
added geometric regression gates for service-bay support, wall closure, gable containment, roof valleys, and absence of duplicate courses

critiqueFindings.finding: The valley flashing continues roughly 1.60 metres beyond the bump-out roof substrate, leaving 89.5% of the apparent main/cross joint unsupported and visibly open.
The dormer eave underside is buried 45 to 50 mm into the front head and gable wall, while the plaster apex also protrudes into the ridge closure.
The independently pitched east end-gable plaster rises about 48 mm through the 48-degree slate skin at the lower-right eave corner.
The fireplace contains only a base, flat fireback, mantel, and point-light glow, with no completed firebox, fuel, ember bed, or visible flame.

decision.reason: The guarded cycle-6 set closes the prior exposure and foundation defects but retains three visible roof-envelope failures and a light-only unfinished hearth.

constructionResponse.summary: Closed the complete roof envelope and replaced the light-only hearth with an authored firebox, crossed fuel, embers, emissive flame geometry, and fire-anchored bounded lighting.
changes: extended the cross-gable roof skins and ridge behind the complete analytic valley so flashing is supported by both weather systems
raised and ridge-capped the dormer roof for 50 mm eave clearance and positive gable-apex cover

added full-bounds roof-substrate, dormer-clearance, end-gable, fuel-orientation, containment, and emissive-fire regression gates

decision.reason: Independent Fable and Opus probes plus strengthened non-GPU production gates close all four cycle-6 findings; visual acceptance still requires guarded native capture and human review.

constructionResponse.summary: Rebuilt the cottage through the engine-owned architectural compiler with staged constraints, layered weather construction, semantic whole-primitive LOD, and runtime-owned distance switching.

critiqueFindings.finding: Object-wide timber projection collapses side faces to a thin texture column, producing severe barcode stretching across portal frames, window frames, fascia, and furnishings.
Oversized full-corner diagonal black cames dominate each opening and read as boarded defensive crosses rather than leaded cottage glazing.
The full-depth opaque soot cavity occludes the authored logs, embers, and flame geometry, leaving a black rectangle lit by an apparently detached practical light.
Gapped and jittered decorative threshold courses read as overlapping fractured slabs instead of one joined tread-and-riser assembly.

decision.reason: The cycle-8 engine capture proves the new structural pipeline but remains below the locked visual floor because of systematic UV collapse, window language, hidden fire, and fractured entrance finish.
